card: Two official classes with two different definitions — and neither of them means "forest".

frame.alt: A single figure on a path through a dense stand of tall pines

answer: In India's official assessment, forest cover is all land over one hectare with tree canopy density above 10 per cent, whatever is growing there and whoever owns it — a plantation counts, an orchard can count. Tree cover is patches smaller than one hectare outside recorded forest, including scattered trees in towns. Neither definition requires a forest ecosystem, and that is why the numbers surprise people.
explainLead: The Forest Survey of India maps canopy from satellite imagery. What it can see is canopy; what it reports are these two classes.
explain: Forest cover is a canopy measure applied to a minimum mapping unit of one hectare at a density threshold of 10 per cent. It is silent on ownership, on legal status and on species. A mango orchard, a eucalyptus plantation, a rubber estate and old-growth sal forest all satisfy it if the canopy is dense enough over a large enough patch.

Tree cover exists because a canopy measure with a one-hectare floor misses an enormous amount of India's actual tree stock — roadside avenues, field boundaries, homestead trees, urban gardens. It is estimated separately, using a different technique, for patches below that floor and outside the recorded forest area.
The two are reported separately and then added into a headline "forest and tree cover" figure. Adding them is legitimate arithmetic. Reading the sum as an ecosystem measure is not.

defs.d: The share of ground shaded by tree crowns. 10 per cent is the floor for forest cover; the classes above it are open, moderately dense and very dense.
Land legally notified as forest. Different from forest cover, and the two are routinely confused.
One hectare. Anything smaller cannot be forest cover, however many trees are on it.

after: There is no limit to break here. This is a definition, and the definition is the finding: a country can add forest cover while losing forest, if what replaces it holds a canopy.

readHead: How to read a forest figure
readLead: Three questions, and most published claims about India's forests fail at least one.
measure: Which class? Forest cover, tree cover, recorded forest area and "forest and tree cover" are four different quantities, and headlines move between them freely.
At what density threshold? 10 per cent is the Indian floor. International datasets commonly use 30 per cent. The same landscape produces different totals under each.
Compared with what? ISFR revises its own previous figure when methods change, so a change is only meaningful against the revised base the report itself publishes. ISFR 2023 gives both.
cannot: It cannot tell you what kind of forest it is. Plantation and primary forest are indistinguishable in a canopy measure.
It cannot tell you about biodiversity, carbon or soil. Canopy is not ecosystem.
It cannot be compared directly with satellite tree-cover-loss series, which measure a different thing at a different threshold — see tree-cover loss.
A national total cannot be disaggregated back to a place. State tables exist for that reason.
